replication.target_description: Hypothesis 1: stimulus (CS+/CS−) by drug group (placebo/L-DOPA) interaction on average SCRs during day-3 spontaneous recovery in extinction context B. Methods explicitly identify this interaction as the major replication effect.

es.location: Results, Effect of L-DOPA administration post extinction on extinction memory retrieval, hypothesis 1, spontaneous recovery; Methods, Sample size (assigned locator p. 4; canonical HTML text unpaginated).
es.quote: Contrary to our predictions, administration of L-DOPA on day 2 did not result in a statistically significant reduction of spontaneous recovery on day 3 (averaged CRs across all trials; stimulus: F 1,53 = 55.30, p < 0.001, generalized η 2 = 0.20; group: F 1,53 = 0.91, p = 0.344; stimulus*group: F 1,53 = 0.02, p = 0.887; n = 55).

notes: Identity verified from the canonical text: title, six named authors, Nature Communications 15, article 2699 (2024), and DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-46936-y match the assigned replication reference. This is the primary published research article web-text parse, with Abstract, Results, Discussion, Methods and article metadata, not a preregistration or secondary report. Linked supplementary files are not supplied. No PDF path was supplied; no PDF rendering performed. Original source is unassigned and has not been inspected. Unassigned fields are placeholders only. Only es_value_r is assigned. The target is identified by the explicit Methods statement specifying the stimulus-by-group interaction, rather than choosing the stimulus or group main effect. Same-test printed p = 0.887, n = 55 are contextual observations only, not assigned fields. Context-C renewal and covariate-adjusted regressions are distinct tests. Target evidence: Our major effect of interest in the discovery study 16 was the interaction effect of stimuli (CS + /CS−) and group (placebo/L-DOPA) on average SCRs during the test in the extinction context on day 3, corresponding to our replication hypothesis 1.
